title: Simple maps
examples: Where is the playground on this map?
What does this little picture mean?
How do we know where the classroom is?

explain.say: A map is a drawing of a place. It shows the place from above.

draw.text: A map: a place seen from above

explain.say: Looking straight down from above is called a bird's-eye view. You see everything at once.
You can draw a map of your classroom. It shows where the tables and the door are.
Maps use small pictures called symbols. A symbol stands for a real thing.
A small drawing of a tree means there is a real tree there.
A map is much smaller than the real place. You use it to find your way.

draw.text: A map helps you find your way

faq.q: What is the difference between a map and a real place?
faq.a: A map is a drawing that shows a real place. It is a picture of the area.
asks: Is a map like a drawing?
Does a map show the real thing?

faq.q: What does a bird's-eye view mean?
faq.a: It means looking down at something from very high up, like from a bird.
asks: How does a bird see the ground?

faq.a: Symbols are small and easy to read. They keep the map tidy and clear.
asks: Why are there little pictures on the map?
What do the symbols stand for?

faq.q: Can we make a map of our school?
faq.a: Yes, we can draw a map of our school grounds. We can put in symbols for the playground.
asks: Can we map the whole school?
What if we map the school?

faq.q: How do I find something on a map?
faq.a: Look for the symbol of the thing you want. Then follow the paths or roads to get there.
asks: How do I find the door on the map?

facts: A map is a drawing of an area.
A bird's-eye view looks down from above.
Symbols are small pictures that stand for things.
A classroom map shows where things are inside.

quiz.say: Think of a park map. Tap where you see the park from.
quiz.why: A map shows a place from above. This is called a bird's-eye view.

wrong.0: From the side, you see the front of things, like a photo of a house.
wrong.2: From very close, you see only one small part of the place.

quiz.say: Look at the symbol on the map. Tap what it stands for.
quiz.why: The tree symbol stands for a real tree in that place.

wrong.0: A house has its own symbol, a small drawing of a house.
wrong.1: A car has its own symbol, a small drawing of a car.

quiz.say: Think of a map of your classroom. Tap what it helps you do.
quiz.why: A classroom map shows where things are, like the door and the tables.

wrong.1: Painting changes the walls, but a map shows where things are.
wrong.2: Counting uses numbers, but a map shows where things are.
